title: PEANuT: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation with Weight-aware Neural Tweakers

problem.claim: Updating all parameters of large pre-trained foundation models is prohibitively expensive.

gap.claim: Existing PEFT methods commonly use weight-agnostic linear approximations that limit expressiveness.

contributions.claim: PEANuT is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning framework using compact weight-aware neural tweakers to generate task-adaptive updates conditioned on frozen pre-trained weights.
PEANuT is claimed to achieve equivalent or greater expressivity than existing linear PEFT methods with comparable or fewer parameters.
PEANuT captures complex update patterns without full model tuning while maintaining computational efficiency.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly propose PEANuT as a novel PEFT framework with weight-aware neural tweakers.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report equivalent or greater expressivity than existing linear PEFT methods with comparable or fewer parameters.
Across four benchmarks and more than twenty datasets, the authors report consistent outperformance of strong baselines in NLP and vision tasks with low computational overhead.

narrative_sequence.summary: Full-parameter fine-tuning is highly effective but prohibitively expensive.
Existing PEFT methods improve efficiency but may lose expressiveness through weight-agnostic linear approximations.
PEANuT introduces weight-aware neural tweakers that condition task-adaptive updates on frozen weights.
The framework is designed to capture complex update patterns efficiently without full model tuning.
The authors report theoretical expressivity results and broad benchmark improvements with low overhead.

source_observation.claim: Task-adaptive updates conditioned on frozen pre-trained weights are reported to improve expressiveness over weight-agnostic linear updates.

interpretation.claim: Using information already present in frozen weights may increase the flexibility of parameter-efficient adaptation.

application.claim: Consider weight-conditioned update modules when linear PEFT approximations are insufficiently expressive.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish performance or efficiency outside the reported NLP and vision benchmarks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the architecture or training procedure of the neural tweakers.
The abstract does not identify the four benchmarks or more than twenty datasets.
The abstract does not provide quantitative performance, parameter, or computational-overhead values.
